source.author: stat
source.text: Talia dum patri canit intemerata sacerdos, illius elatis tremefacta assurgere vittis canities tenuesque impelli sanguine vultus, nec iam firmanti baculo nec virgine fida nititur, erectusque solo desiste canendo.
source.text_original: ' / Talia dum patri canit intemerata sacerdos, / illius elatis tremefacta assurgere vittis / canities tenuesque impelli sanguine vultus, / nec iam firmanti baculo nec virgine fida / nititur, erectusque solo 'desiste canendo.
source.text_english: While the spotless priestess sings such things to her father, his white hair, raised by his lifted fillets, begins to tremble and his thin cheeks are stirred by the blood; now he leans neither on the staff that supports him nor on the faithful maiden, and, rising from the ground, he says, “Stop singing.”

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus:
reuse.text_original: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus / extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque / talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus: /
reuse.text_english: and now Cretheus had lifted his faint face to the song, and, looking with sorrow upon both son and daughter-in-law, was opening his lips to say such things, with his blood already poured out:
